steps.label: Write the form of a plane parallel to the ZX-plane
steps.margin_note: First mark. The ZX-plane is the plane on which every point has y = 0. Parallel planes share a normal, so a plane parallel to it must also have the Y-axis as its normal.
steps.memory_tip: The ZX-plane is y = 0: the letter missing from its name is the coordinate that stays zero.

steps.why: The ZX-plane holds the Z-axis and the X-axis, so the coordinate that is missing from its name is the one that stays 0 on it. Planes parallel to it fix that same coordinate at some other value.
common_mistakes: Writing the ZX-plane as x = 0 or z = 0.
Letting x or z appear in the answer, which would tilt the plane.

Writing y = 0 by copying the ZX-plane instead of the parallel plane through the point.
